column1: # *** ON PRIVACY. *** The test belongs to a LIVING descendant - a granddaughter of Pablo Armando, and a

# HER POSITION IN THE DESCENT: she is one quarter Pablo Armando. Her other three grandparents are
# Mary Septima Taylor (English, of Devon and Suffolk) and two Booyzens (Cape Afrikaner).

column2: At LOW confidence the count goes to 8/8. Five are legible: South Africa; South Africa and Zimbabwe; Argentina (Corrientes and Buenos Aires), Uruguay and Paraguay; England; Ireland (Cork, Kerry and Limerick) and England. Three remain below the fold and have not been seen.
column3: *** NO ITALIAN GROUP APPEARS AMONG THE FIVE. *** The two South African groups fit the Booyzen half and the family's spread into the Transvaal; the two British-Isles groups fit Mary Septima Taylor. The Rio de la Plata group remains the only one that can come from Pablo Armando.
*** NONE AT ALL. *** If Pablo Armando had been a Spanish-descended criollo, roughly 25% would be expected in a granddaughter.

Her other three grandparents are English and Cape Afrikaner. Italian ancestry has no other plausible source in her tree. At one quarter, 11.1% in her implies roughly 44% in him - about one Italian parent.
Northern-dominant, which is the signature of the Ligurian and Piedmontese emigration that made Rosario the most Italian city in Argentina.
